case_name: Smt. Mukul Ray v. Sri Samar Bijoy Roy — FAT 638 of 2015
facts_of_case: The wife appealed against the trial court's decision to grant divorce on grounds of irretrievable breakdown of marriage. The husband had proved existence of grounds under clauses (ia) and (ib) in sub-section(1) of section 13, Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. However, the decree for divorce was granted.

legal_principles.principle: Continuance of a marriage that is irretrievably broken down can itself amount to cruelty.
legal_principles.held: The Supreme Court in Satish Sitole (supra) had said, continuance of marriage irretrievably broken down could itself amount to cruelty.

legal_principles.principle: A party's assertion of regular co-habitation with full satisfaction can be inferred from their pleading and evidence.
legal_principles.held: Meaningful reading of above evidence and the pleading would cause conclusion or inference that his client was always ready and willing to cohabit with her husband.

legal_principles.principle: A court may grant a decree of divorce to put quietus to all litigations between the parties and to save them from further agony.
legal_principles.held: The Supreme Court in Manish Goel vs. Rohini Goel reported in (2010) 4 SCC 393 had granted decree of divorce to put quietus to all litigations between the parties and to save them from further agony.

keywords: Vishnu Dutt Sharma vs. Manju Sharma
